text:
Chloe Martin: quick review request on approvals/abort API + audit event shape for Dedicated staged rollouts. PR draft is up but before we bake it in. main open: RBAC scopes for enterprise tenants + what goes into audit log.

Ethan Park: +1. esp want to lock down stage approval flow. we’ve had too many “approve twice / race with evaluator tick” edge cases.

Benji Okafor: current API sketch (rough):
- `POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}:approve` body `{ stage_id, comment }`
- `POST /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}:abort` body `{ reason, rollback_to_stage_id? }`
- both return updated rollout status + `approval_event_id`
- requires `Idempotency-Key` header
but I’m not sure if we want `:approve` scoped to stage vs overall plan.

Hannah Rivera: from Console POV, we approve *current stage* (the one in `WAITING_FOR_APPROVAL`). if we let callers pass arbitrary stage_id, we need to validate it’s the next stage + not already completed.

Jordan Lee: routing/policy needs approvals to be deterministic + serializable. I’d strongly prefer server decides which stage is “approvable” based on rollout state machine, and the API is basically “approve next step”. otherwise we’ll get weird calls approving stage 3 while stage 1 is still running.

Chloe Martin: so: `POST ...:approve` with no stage_id? and server approves whatever is pending?

Felix Schneider: +1, it simplifies audit UX too (“approved stage 2” computed from state). but we should still include `stage_id` in the response/event so UI can show exactly what happened.

Benji Okafor: ok, then request body becomes `{ comment }` only. maybe optional `expected_stage_id` for optimistic concurrency? like “approve only if pending stage == X”.

Ethan Park: yeah some “if-match” semantics would be nice. we already have plan_version + status_version. could do header `If-Match: status_version`.

Jordan Lee: I like `If-Match` on `rollout.status_version` (or whatever we call it). otherwise two operators smash approve and we advance twice.

Hannah Rivera: console can send `If-Match` easily.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: jumping in on RBAC scope. we need to answer: can an enterprise tenant do approvals themselves? if yes, is it at tenant scope or pool scope? and what about “Redwood operator override”.

Chloe Martin: for beta we were thinking: allowlist tenants, then tenant admins can approve/abort for their pools. but Redwood SRE needs break-glass abort always.

Marcus Lin: security view: we should separate permissions:
- `rollout.approve`
- `rollout.abort`
- `rollout.edit`
with scopes:
- `tenant:{tenant_id}` for customer users
- `operator` for Redwood internal
and make sure audit captures both actor + scope used.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: +1. Implementation wise we already have principal types `user`, `service`, `operator`. For enterprise, `user` is within tenant. For Redwood internal, it’s `operator` with global scope.

Benji Okafor: question: do we need a permission for “view audit events”? or inherit from pool read.

Marcus Lin: audit events are sensitive-ish but for the tenant they’re their own change mgmt records. I’d make “view rollout audit” gated by `rollout.read` or pool admin. We can iterate; minimum is: only principals who can see the pool can list its audit.

Kevin Osei: audit export pipeline expects stable event names + common fields. please don’t invent a bespoke schema per feature. we should emit into the existing `audit_log_events` stream with:
- `event_type`
- `actor_id`, `actor_type`
- `tenant_id`
- `resource_type`, `resource_id`
- `request_id`
- `occurred_at`
plus `metadata` (but note: metadata is string->string; no nested objects)

Felix Schneider: console uses the audit stream to render “who approved”. so event should include readable fields in metadata: `pool_id`, `rollout_id`, `plan_version`, `stage_id`, `stage_name`, `decision`.

Chloe Martin: careful: we can’t put too much PII. actor display name comes from identity service when rendering. audit should store actor id.

Kevin Osei: yep. and please include `impersonated_by` if we do support impersonation. (not sure we do for Dedicated yet).

Kaitlyn Nguyen: we do have “operator acting on behalf of tenant” in admin tooling sometimes. If we’re going to allow it for rollouts, it MUST be explicit and logged.

Marcus Lin: +1. If operator is using a tenant-scoped token, we need an `actor_type=operator` + `acting_as=tenant_user` or similar. Otherwise customers will see “user X approved” when it was actually Redwood.

Jordan Lee: on abort: do we need both “abort rollout” vs “rollback now”? abort could mean “stop progressing” and keep current routing weights, which is dangerous.

Ethan Park: good call. for Dedicated, abort should be safe-by-default: set target weights back to baseline and mark rollout ABORTED. i.e. “abort == rollback to previous stable plan” (or at least “drain to 0% new stage”).

Hannah Rivera: UI copy also assumes abort == revert. otherwise customers will be confused.

Benji Okafor: technically we have three actions:
1) pause/hold (system)
2) abort (human)
3) rollback (explicit)
but if abort triggers rollback, we may not need separate rollback endpoint v1.

Chloe Martin: product wants one button: Abort (and it rolls back). if we need “stop but don’t rollback” that’s internal only and should not be exposed to tenants.

Marcus Lin: +1. a tenant shouldn’t be able to put system into ambiguous “half rolled” state.

Jordan Lee: ok, then API `:abort` will: set desired state = ABORTING, routing transitions back to stable, then ABORTED when complete. include progress in status.

Ethan Park: approvals API should be similar: set desired state = ADVANCING, then stage transitions by evaluator/controller. avoid synchronous multi-step.

Felix Schneider: on audit events, what do we emit for auto-holds? SRE asked for “auto-hold due to missing metrics” to be auditable too.

Kevin Osei: please emit system-generated audit events too (`actor_type=service`, `actor_id=gate-evaluator`). that’s common.

Marcus Lin: and for approvals, include whether it was manual or auto. v1 is manual approvals but auto-hold/auto-rollback are system actions.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: RBAC edge: can tenant “approve” but not “abort”? we probably want to allow both for tenant admin. for beta, simplest: `tenant_role=DedicatedAdmin` gets `rollout.approve` + `rollout.abort`.

Chloe Martin: agreed. we can add more granular later.

Benji Okafor: naming: do we go with RPC-ish `:approve` style or classic REST `POST /approvals`?

Ethan Park: we’re already using google-ish style in other control plane APIs. keep `:approve` + `:abort`.

Jordan Lee: please ensure idempotency covers retries. if customer hits approve twice with same key, return same event id.

Hannah Rivera: console will send `Idempotency-Key` + `If-Match`. if `If-Match` fails, we show “rollout advanced, refresh”.

Felix Schneider: audit listing endpoint: `GET /v1/dedicated/pools/{pool_id}/rollouts/{rollout_id}/audit-events?page_size=...&page_token=...`.

Kevin Osei: ok but make sure page_token is opaque string. and event payload fields are strings.

Marcus Lin: last thing: event types. propose:
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.created`
- `dedicated.rollout_plan.updated`
- `dedicated.rollout.approved`
- `dedicated.rollout.aborted`
- `dedicated.rollout.held`
- `dedicated.rollout.auto_rollback`
with resource `resource_type=dedicated_rollout` and `resource_id=rollout_id`.

Chloe Martin: works for me. we’ll include `pool_id` in metadata.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: and enforce that tenant principals can only act on pools in their tenant. operator can act on any pool. any “operator acting on behalf” must be explicit and logged.

Ethan Park: cool. action items:
- Benji update approve endpoint: no stage_id; optional `If-Match` support
- Jordan confirm abort semantics with routing
- Kaitlyn/Marcus finalize permission mapping + break-glass operator override
- Kevin align event schema w audit pipeline constraints

Benji Okafor: ack. I’ll push updated API spec today.

Marcus Lin: ping me on the PR for the RBAC bits. want to make sure the tenant scope check happens before state mutation.

Kevin Osei: and please add a couple example audit events in the PR description (as flattened key/values). helps reviewers.

Chloe Martin: will do. thanks all.
